items.essay: Some people believe cities should spend more money on public transport than on roads. I agree because reliable buses and trains can carry many people using less space. However, investment should be based on demand: smaller towns may need safer roads before they can support frequent services.

Technology has changed how children learn. Online lessons give students access to useful material, but they cannot replace every benefit of a classroom. A teacher can notice confusion and encourage discussion. Schools should therefore combine digital resources with direct teaching rather than choosing only one method.

In my opinion governments must protect historical buildings even when land is expensive. Old buildings show how a community developed and can attract visitors. This does not mean every structure should remain untouched; authorities should assess its importance and consider safe adaptation when possible.

Many employees prefer working from home because it saves commuting time. Nevertheless, remote work can make collaboration harder for new staff. Companies should offer flexible arrangements and create regular opportunities for colleagues to meet. The best policy depends on the work and the needs of employees.

Advertising encourages people to buy things they do not need. This is sometimes true, especially when adverts create pressure through unrealistic lifestyles. Yet advertising also helps customers compare products and discover small businesses. Better consumer education is more effective than banning all commercial messages.

Universities should teach practical skills as well as academic theory. Graduates often understand concepts but struggle to apply them in a workplace. Internships and project-based courses can address this gap. However, universities should not become training centres for one employer; critical thinking remains essential.

Some argue that museums should be free. Free entry makes culture accessible to families who cannot afford expensive activities. On the other hand, museums need stable funding to maintain collections. Governments could subsidise permanent exhibitions while charging modest fees for special events.

I think children should learn a musical instrument at school. Music develops patience and gives pupils another way to express ideas. It may also improve cooperation when students play together. Schools should provide different instruments and avoid judging children only by their technical ability.

Traffic congestion is mainly caused by too many private cars. Building additional roads can offer short-term relief, but it may encourage more people to drive. Cities should improve public transport, walking routes and cycling facilities. These measures give residents realistic alternatives to car travel.

People disagree about whether success depends more on talent or hard work. Natural ability can make learning easier, but it rarely guarantees achievement. Consistent practice helps people identify weaknesses and improve. In most fields, opportunity and support also influence how far a person can progress.

The government should spend more on preventing illness than treating it. Public information, vaccinations and accessible exercise facilities can reduce pressure on hospitals. However, prevention cannot remove the need for good treatment. A balanced health budget should support both early intervention and high-quality medical care.

International tourism creates jobs, but it can damage local environments. Popular destinations may experience waste, noise and rising housing costs. Authorities should limit visitor numbers in fragile areas and ensure tourism income benefits residents. Responsible planning is preferable to rejecting tourism completely.

Some people say public libraries are no longer necessary because information is online. This view ignores people without reliable internet and the value of quiet study spaces. Libraries also help users assess information. They should modernise their services while continuing to provide books and community facilities.

Schools should start later in the morning. Teenagers often find it difficult to concentrate very early, and a later start may improve attendance. However, changing school hours affects parents and transport. Authorities should test flexible schedules and evaluate the results before making a universal change.

A city should preserve parks even when it needs more housing. Green spaces improve health and provide places where neighbours can meet. The housing shortage is serious, but it can be addressed through better use of existing land and higher-quality buildings rather than removing every park.

The chart compares the proportion of commuters using cars, buses and bicycles in a town in 2000 and 2020. Overall, car use fell while cycling became more common. Cars remained the largest category in both years, although the gap between cars and buses narrowed considerably.

The table shows monthly household spending in three categories. Housing accounted for the largest share throughout the period, whereas entertainment represented the smallest. Food expenditure changed only slightly, suggesting that the main shift in household budgets occurred in housing costs.

The process illustrates how recycled paper is produced. First, used paper is collected and sorted. It is then mixed with water to create pulp, which is cleaned to remove unwanted material. Finally, the pulp is pressed and dried into new sheets that can be used again.

The two maps show a coastal village before and after redevelopment. The most noticeable change is the addition of a hotel and a larger road near the beach. Several houses were replaced by visitor facilities, while the harbour remained in the same location.

The line graph presents changes in electricity consumption over one day. Demand was lowest during the early morning, then increased sharply as people began their daily activities. It reached a second peak in the evening before declining towards midnight.
